cards.title: Vd1 replacement • p2≤1/2
cards.hypothesis: An away Vd1 supplier has a center-free shared edge. Replacement preserves the skeleton, not necessarily H or gap rank.
cards.construction: BEFORE shows the original genuine Vd1 supplier: one outside vertex, one adjacent positive trace, and a 15-degree departure from the nearest hex-axis orientation. Its short crossing is magnified. Then the old supplier is removed, the first replacement is shown, and the second is added. Use p1=0.20, p2=0.33 and epsilon=0.02. The AFTER triangles are deliberately axis-aligned Vd0, each with boundary sum 0.98.
cards.argument: Both new actual boundary sums equal 1−epsilon=0.98; both roles have no adjacent support. With the scalar margins verified, the replacement removes the unique supercritical role, contradicting N0.
cards.scope: The original Vd1 supplier is a real local triangle; its actual incoming and own-radial reaches are used in the scalar margins. The partner demands B=0.20 and r=0.52 are explicitly stipulated, not asserted to come from a jointly realized covering configuration. Both replacements preserve the displayed supplier traces. Vd2 is not silently substituted into this Vd1 lemma; its separate clip leads to the perimeter obstruction.

cards.title: Zero gaps, N+≥2 • cyclic area loss
cards.hypothesis: Zero-gap area branch: cyclic selected demands (a_i,b_i)=(1−x_{i−1},x_i). This example has exactly two selected sums a_i+b_i>1. Those selected counts must not be called actual N+ for six original covering roles.
cards.construction: Use the actual AREA CONJ mode with high search quality. Move all six shared handoffs by 0.58: x_i=t+[0,0.04,0.02,0.06,0.03,0.01]_i, with t from 0.16 to 0.74. Watch the six optimized candidate triangles, the native six-row f_i/loss table, and the native totals. The companion MAX AREA clip explains the single-row optimization.
cards.argument: The proof bounds the sum of the true local maxima by an exact area-loss argument. The app instead displays best-found candidates: its f_i estimates are lower bounds on maxima and its 1−f_i estimates are upper bounds on minimum losses. A displayed sum below 5 is therefore explanatory, not an independent certificate.
cards.scope: Genuine Area Conj controls and optimizer rendering. Native displayed results are checked against the pinned algorithm and polygon clipping. These independently optimized closed local triangles are not claimed to constitute an open boundary cover. The previous Free-mode boundary-only clip has been replaced.

cards.title: Max Area • how one local area loss is obtained
cards.hypothesis: Given one vertex and prescribed adjacent anchors a,b, search closed unit equilateral triangles containing these three points. The local maximal inside area is normalized by sqrt(3)/4.
cards.construction: Use the actual MAX AREA mode, with its native a,b inputs, high-quality search, optimal candidate rendering and native f(a,b), 1−f(a,b) readouts. Sweep a from 0.08 to 0.57 and b from 0.12 to 0.56. The triangle and lost-area shape change substantially rather than oscillating imperceptibly.
cards.argument: This is the local optimization repeated in each of the six Area Conj rows. Larger prescribed anchors restrict the feasible family. The exact proof supplies the universal upper bound; a finite search supplies a realizing candidate and a numerical estimate only.
cards.scope: The saved JSON is an AREA CONTROL RECIPE, not an importable Controller or Free snapshot: the app does not serialize these mode inputs. Set the listed a,b values and quality manually, or replay them with capture.py. No T3-like constraint is imposed on the optimizer.
